## Research Ideas

Idea One:\
I want to continue what I did in the spring with either more sports and comparing the ages with best success while also implementing training and testing with my past model as well as checking accuracy of my past model (AUC, ROC, Confusion Matrix, etc.) I also want to add variables into my F1 model from the spring such as how often a driver switched teams( whether they've been on one team their entire career or like 5). ## Exploratory Data Analysis

The following EDA covers data in Formula One, NASCAR, and MotoGP.

### Formula One

The scatter plot below demonstrates the relationship between Formula One driver's age and the points they get in a season. We see a non-linear relationship between the points with a peak from the loess curve applied to the plot appearing at a little over thirty years of age.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
F1_data |>
  ggplot(aes(driver_age, driver_points)) + geom_jitter(alpha = 0.5, size = 3) + stat_smooth() + labs(title = "Relationship Between Age and Success in F1", 
       x = "Age" , y = "Points")
```
In Formula One constructors, or teams, are often referred to as top, midfield, or bottom teams. To recreate this and not create the grouping through bias by selecting the perceived "top teams" I did a one dimensional Jenks clustering analysis on the total points a team has for each season. The number of clusters, k, were predetermined to be 3, to mimic the three groups teams are put into in F1. In the table output of the cluster groups we see that the bottom teams have minimum points of 0 and maximum points of 202. The middle teams have minimum points of 275 and maximum points of 522. The top teams have minimum points of 554 and maximum points of 860. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

F1_data |>
  group_by(team_group) |>
  summarise(
    Team_Count = n(),
    Min_Points = min(constructor_points, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max_Points = max(constructor_points, na.rm = TRUE),
    Avg_Points = mean(constructor_points, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "F1 Team Grouping"
  )
```

The violin plots below show the distribution of the table output from above.


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

F1_data |>
  ggplot(aes(y = constructor_points, x = team_group, col = team_group, fill = team_group)) + geom_violin(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Team Groups and Distribution of Points Among Them", x = "Team Group", y = "Total Team Points") + 
  coord_flip()

```

## Modeling

The two main models used are generalized additive models with and without a team group random effect.

$$ \text{Points} = \alpha  + \text{u}_{\text{Driver}_i} + \text{v}_{\text{Team Group}_i}+ f_1(\text{Age}_i) + f_2(\text{Years At Team}_i) + \epsilon_i $$
